open_issues: OWNER RULING NEEDED (the review's last low finding, deliberately left uncoded): src/Wakeel.Core/Services/CoreAr.cs holds this package's user-facing Arabic instead of src/Wakeel.Design/Text/Ar.*.cs. Core is referenced BY Design and UI, so it cannot reference Design without inverting the layering, and Core genuinely must emit finished Arabic (notification rows are persisted; health cards carry «رسالة عربية» and are exported as a text report). Either ratify CoreAr.cs as the Core-layer equivalent of Ar.*.cs and say so in ARCHITECTURE.md §12, or move the sentences to Wakeel.Design/Text/Ar.Core.cs and have the UI resolve them from the stable English ids Core already exposes (HealthComponents / HealthActions / NotificationKinds). No code change made either way.

SCANNER SEVERITY decided from the mockup, not from the owner: W12 (design/exports/preview/light/W) renders a missing scanner as «عطل» with «إعادة الاكتشاف», so CheckScannerAsync now returns HealthStatus.Error rather than Warning; the reasoning is recorded in the method's remarks and in the renamed test. If the owner considers an absent scanner merely degraded, flipping it back is a one-line change plus two assertions.

SyncWarningDays = 3 is my choice, not a spec number. The spec names no staleness threshold for «آخر مزامنة»; 3 days is deliberately shorter than BackupWarningDays (7) and documented as such. The owner may want a different figure.

Still outside this package (unchanged from round 2): nothing calls IClockGuard.StartAsync(now, dispatcher) or IReminderScheduler.Start(ticker, dispatcher), and nothing calls Stop() on sign-out/lock — the sibling B2 screens/shell package must wire them, passing ComponentBase.InvokeAsync as the BackgroundPassDispatcher. ClockCheckTrigger.Import is implemented and tested but has no caller; the sync/import package must call IClockGuard.CheckAsync(ClockCheckTrigger.Import, now, importedDeviceTimestamps).

The four Windows probes (Word registry, WIA scanner, disk, WebView2) still have no unit tests: tests/Wakeel.Core.Tests targets net10.0 and cannot reference the net10.0-windows host, and adding a test project would require editing Wakeel.slnx. All four ran for real during the host boot.
notes:
Every finding addressed; the only one left uncoded is the CoreAr.cs placement, which the review itself said must not change without an owner ruling.

MEDIUM — PartyAr blank for commitments and cases (the one in-scope missing spec item). AttentionService.ReadAllAsync now projects c.PartyId for commitments and for cases, records (row index, party id) as each row is appended via a local Remember(...), and after the six reads resolves them in ONE query — FillPartyNamesAsync: db.Parties.AsNoTracking().Where(p => ids.Contains(p.Id)).Select(p => new { p.Id, p.Name }).ToDictionaryAsync — patching rows with `items[i] with { PartyAr = name }`. A row whose party row is gone keeps null rather than a placeholder. Decisions have no party column in DATA-MODEL, so they remain null by necessity (noted in the code). New test ACommitmentAndACase_CarryTheirPartysName_SoTheGihaColumnIsNotBlank covers a named party on a commitment and a case plus a commitment with no party that must stay null. Measured cost of the extra query: attention-snapshot 47 ms vs 48 ms before — [b2-services] rows=10000 seed=1446ms attention-snapshot=47ms badges-refresh=51ms attention-counts=43ms budget=200ms.

LOW — notification table. New migration src/Wakeel.Core/Migrations/0002_notification_indexes.sql (0001 untouched) adds ix_notifications_source(source, created_at) and ix_notifications_created_at. RunOnceAsync's pre-load is narrowed to `n.Source.StartsWith(KeyPrefix) && n.CreatedAt >= keyFloor`. Added ReminderScheduler.SweepAsync, which deletes only DISMISSED notifications older than KeyRetention — undismissed rows are never touched at any age, and Lookback is far shorter than the floor so no pass can still need a swept key. Two new tests (the sweep keeps an old undismissed row and a recent dismissed one, drops only the old dismissed one; a non-reminder source at the same instant does not suppress a reminder). Because a second migration now ships, SchemaTests.Open_RecordsSchemaVersionOne (which hard-coded 1) became Open_RecordsEveryEmbeddedSchemaVersion, deriving the expected version and row count from the embedded scripts, plus a new Open_IndexesTheNotificationSourceAndCreationTime.

LOW — ClockGuard cancellation. ClockGuard now mirrors TimeProviderMinuteTicker exactly: a CancellationTokenSource created inside the lock in StartAsync after a new private StopCore(), its token passed to the interval CheckAsync, a separate `catch (OperationCanceledException)`, and cancel + dispose + null in StopCore(), which Stop() and Dispose() go through. Three new tests using the existing ManualTimeProvider and a new RecordingClockCheckService that captures the token each call received: Stop cancels the in-flight pass's token; a second Start cancels the first binding's token, leaves exactly one live timer and hands the new tick a live token; a cancelled tick does not tear the timer down.

LOW — privacy. CheckSyncAsync projects only { Kind, LastSyncAt }; EmployeeName is gone. New test TheSyncCard_NeverNamesAnEmployee asserts the seeded employee name appears neither in the card message nor anywhere in ExportText(report).

LOW — W12 card statuses. I viewed design/exports/preview/light/W/W12 once: the scanner card is «عطل» with «إعادة الاكتشاف», and «آخر مزامنة» is «تحذير». CheckScannerAsync now returns HealthStatus.Error (action id stays ConnectScanner — the screen renders it «إعادة الاكتشاف» — with the reasoning in the method's remarks). New const HealthService.SyncWarningDays = 3, documented as deliberately shorter than BackupWarningDays; the newest LastSyncAt across trusted devices older than that now returns Warning + HealthActions.OpenSync with the new CoreAr.HealthSyncOld(details) («…؛ آخر مزامنة قديمة»). Tests: a device last synced 10 days ago warns with OpenSync; one inside the threshold stays Ok with no «قديمة»; the two existing scanner assertions updated to Error.

LOW — health prune vs insert. PersistAsync opens a transaction when db.Database.CurrentTransaction is null, does SaveChangesAsync FIRST, then the ExecuteDeleteAsync prune, then commits, disposing in a finally — the same shape as QuickCaptureService.CaptureExpenseAsync, and a caller-owned transaction keeps its ownership.

LOW — UTC day counts. New internal AttentionService.BackupAgeInDays(lastBackupAt, utcNow, zone?) converts both sides to the local zone before .Date and clamps at 0. It is now the single place the backup age is computed: ReadBackupStateAsync, ReminderScheduler's backupAgeDays (passing the pass's zone) and HealthService.CheckBackupAsync (which had the same UTC bug and was not in the finding) all call it. New test TheBackupAge_IsTheSameEarlyInTheLocalMorningAsItIsLaterTheSameDay seeds a backup seven local days back and asserts DaysSince == 7 and Overdue at both 01:00 and 09:00 local on the same local day.
